questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking, good university, far from Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Toronto in the fall is great - you get a long summer, beautiful fall and taste of the snow in december.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Okay. UofT has a lot of websides so it can take som time to find the information. But most of it is at the webside and otherwise you can always email them (then they answer pretty quickly)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome event in the first week - and then I was lucky to have a house with housemates who helped me with all my small questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was recommended to check-out Campus-coop - they have about 20 houses in Toronto. It is quite cheap (3500dkk/month) and you get to meet new people from all around the world. The danes have a good reputation so if you apply and stress out that you are from Denmark, it might be possible to secure a spot.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is great. If you can find a good spot then you are more flexible. But I would recommend to find a place as close to campus as possible - that was great to be able to grab a beer with other students and just walk around

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They help you with sending out the deadlines and reminders on mail - I was way more stressed than i had needed to be.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You apply and then you have to upload a language test around March. You can not choose courses before May/June, so when you aplly for the "forhåndsgodkendelse" you just have to checkout the courses from former years. 

When you apply for courses, you do it through a google survey link.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email them and there was some Q&A websides

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 3/5 at first round. Some of the 4th year courses I applied for had a limited amount of spots so I did not get them. But you can also get bachelor credits for 200 and 300 level courses (and they are often easier). So in 2nd round, i found some other good courses. There is also a 3rd round of course choosing.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just relax - they always find a solution with KU. Perhaps email UofT directly after you have filled out the google survey link; that helped me once.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good level, interesting and not to difficult

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 3 bachelor courses and one course that I got credited as a Master course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way more like a danish "gymnasie" with participation grades and smaller assignments through the semester. The grading scale goes from 1-100 and you need 50 to pass. So you can check out in the syllabus how many points, each category counts.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POL358H-F: Conflicts, Minority Rights and Para-States in Europe (valgfag)

POL 311 – Law and Political Development (DAK3/valgfag)

POL 218H1F - State, Society, and Power in Comparative Perspective (DAK3/valgfag)

POL354 - POLITICS AND SOCIETY IN RUSSIA (Valgfag/MA credit)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: POL354 and POL358H was great as they were way more in detail (more practical politics and less theories) with a topic than the ones we usually have at KU.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Bike annual plan (able to use all the tourist bikes around the city) for 80CAD as a student - saved me a lot on public transport.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cheaper to get coffees and eat out. Grocery stores are almost the same as Denmark. Fruit and greens are cheap in Chinatown

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of free services; gym, swimming pool, clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Outdoor club, lots of different sport activities (you can join for free)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the Varsity centre run track and athletic centre swim pool

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel a lot. Algonquin national park can be done as a long daytrip in the fall (so beautiful, but rent a car with other people). Ottawa and Montreal as a combined weekend trip with bus/Via rail. Vancouver and Whistler in the holidays. And then USA is so close with 1,5 hour planes to NYC and Washington. 

Of course also Niagara Falls as a day trip with bus/train (pretty cheap).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: no problems - the Canadians are friendly

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get to join events that are not just for exchange students. Find a community; like a university club or a church (they are so friendly) and introduce yourself, then they will give you a warm welcome

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In class people do not know each other as well as in Denmark. So it can be a bit silent. But if you talk to people, they will most likely respond kindly and engage in conversations.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Canadian kindness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Campus Coop for housing
2. Try to meet local canadian people
2,5. Travel a lot - get to see the American continent, as it will never be as easy as now
3. Buy fruit and greens in Chinatown (saves money for travels;))

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of courses, so you will no matter what find something that is interesting (even if you do not get your 1st priority)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improved my English and got to travel a lot - and have the opportunity to be at a top25 University with a lot of good professors and cool buildings.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not that many challenges. But perhaps the time before travelling without knowing what it would be like.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
